name: Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle ITR-5 'Ashmaker'
description:
The Ionic Thermoclastic Rifle functions by projecting a sustained stream of superheated ionized gas — technically a directed plasma jet — at ranges far exceeding conventional flamethrower technology. The key innovation is the magnetic confinement collar at the barrel's terminus, a toroidal field generator that compresses the plasma stream into a coherent column and prevents the lateral thermal bleed that makes conventional plasma projection impractical at range. The result is a weapon that delivers extreme thermal energy to a target at distances up to 60 meters with a column diameter of approximately 8 centimeters at point of impact.

Developed by TESSERA CORPONATION under a military infrastructure contract, the ITR-5 was originally intended for demolition work — specifically for cutting through reinforced structural elements in contested urban environments. Its adoption as a direct combat weapon was, by TESSERA's own internal communications, 'an unanticipated market development.' The weapon's effect on unarmored biological targets is severe and rapid: the plasma column causes flash vaporization of surface tissue and ignition of underlying structures within 2 seconds of sustained contact. Armored targets experience accelerated surface ablation and heat transfer sufficient to cause incapacitation through cookoff of interior equipment.

The Ashmaker has a complex cultural footprint. Its association with demolition work gives it a certain blue-collar credibility in the construction and infrastructure sectors, where modified civilian variants are not uncommon for cutting operations. Its use as a weapon is associated primarily with large-scale violence — building clearances, punitive actions by corporate security against squatter communities — and it carries a stigma that most individual operators find professionally undesirable. Carrying one signals either professional demolition work or a willingness to engage in atrocity.
specifications:
effective range: 60m (combat), 15m (industrial cutting)
plasma temperature: 4,200°C at emitter, 2,800°C at 60m
column diameter: 8 cm at 60m
fuel source: TESSERA T-Gas Canister TGC-4 (45-second continuous burn per canister)
weight: 6.8 kg (empty), 9.2 kg (full canister)
length: 91 cm
confinement collar: Toroidal magnetic field generator, 0.3-second spool-up
cooling: Forced-air radiative system, 40-second mandatory cooldown after 15-second sustained burn
tactical_use: Military operators use the ITR-5 for bunker denial, fortification clearing, and area denial in enclosed spaces where the thermal environment becomes a weapon in itself. Combat engineers use it for rapid structural cutting under fire. Against personnel, operators typically use short bursts rather than sustained streams to manage fuel consumption and cooldown cycles. The weapon's size and fuel requirements make it a two-person system in sustained operations — one operator, one reload carrier.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's construction sector, the ITR-5's industrial variant is a common tool — TESSERA has successfully normalized it as a precision demolition instrument. Workers in the Palladian Construction sphere carry them as standard equipment. The combat variant exists in a different moral register entirely. Its use in the Colvert District clearance operations four years ago — where TESSERA corporate security used ITR-5s to evict and 'sanitize' squatter warrens — left a deep scar in collective memory. The weapon's nickname 'Ashmaker' originated from survivors of that event.
known_users: Survivors of the Colvert clearance (as symbol, not users)
story_hooks: A TESSERA internal memo has surfaced describing the Colvert clearance operation as a 'field demonstration' of the ITR-5's combat capabilities. Someone leaked it. TESSERA wants it back. The leaker wants it published.
A series of infrastructure sabotage events shows the distinctive cutting pattern of an ITR-5. The targets are all TESSERA-affiliated construction sites. Someone is using their own tool against them.

An industrial variant ITR-5 has been modified for combat and used in three separate murders in the upper districts. The modification is sophisticated — not a field hack. Someone with engineering access is building weapons.
A community in the lower districts has acquired two ITR-5s as a deterrent against corporate clearance operations. They've announced their possession publicly. TESSERA is deciding how to respond.
related_entities: Grave Protocol Arms Terminus GPA-1 'Last Rites'

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist energy weapon with a distinctly industrial aesthetic — part demolition tool, part military instrument. The ITR-5 presents as a chunky, purposeful rifle with an oversized barrel assembly and prominent toroidal field generator at the muzzle. The silhouette reads 'heavy infrastructure' rather than sleek lethality, with a center-of-gravity bias toward the barrel that makes it appear perpetually aimed downward.
physical_description.dimensions: 91 cm overall length. Barrel assembly extends 28 cm from receiver. Toroidal magnetic collar at terminus measures 12 cm in diameter × 8 cm depth. Magazine well accommodates TGC-4 canisters at rear. Stock-to-muzzle sight line approximately 8 cm above centerline.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and forward-heavy — 6.8 kg empty feels like handling a loaded fire axe. With full TGC-4 canister (9.2 kg total), the weapon demands both hands and a firm stance. The weight is honest rather than elegant, distributing toward the barrel where the plasma generation and confinement systems live. Balanced for two-handed shouldering, not one-handed spray.
physical_description.primary_material: Steel reinforced polymer composite frame. Barrel and confinement assembly are matte-finished steel with internal copper coil windings visible through inspection ports. The toroidal collar is brushed titanium alloy with visible electromagnetic shielding. Magazine well is injection-molded polymer rated for thermal stress.
physical_description.finish: Utilitarian matte black with extensive heat-stress patination — surface shows thermal bloom marks, oil-staining around the radiator vents, and micro-scratches from industrial deployment. The titanium collar has a worn brushed appearance with faint oxidation discoloration. Wear patterns concentrate around the barrel's exhaust ports where plasma bleed occurs during operation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with brushed titanium/silver toroidal collar. Accent colors include burnt orange heat-discoloration streaks around the radiative cooling fins, and faint warning-yellow paint on the two-position safety lever. TESSERA corporation branding appears in gray stencil.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with aggressive diagonal texturing — designed for pressure-gloved handling. The foregrip is wrapped in heat-resistant cord binding in several places where previous operators reinforced it. The charging handle is knurled bare steel, cold to the touch even after thermal operation.
distinctive_features: Toroidal magnetic field generator ring at barrel terminus — glows faint blue-white when powered
Eight radiative cooling fins running the length of the barrel, stained with heat oxidation
Transparent inspection ports showing copper induction coils winding around the plasma chamber
Two-position safety lever in warning yellow, positioned for thumb operation
Pressure gauge on right side showing fuel canister status (red zone clearly marked)
Exhaust port vents with articulating heat shielding to prevent lateral thermal bleed
Reinforced magazine well with thermal stress indicators (color-change polymer)
Burnt-orange discoloration bloom around exhaust ports and radiator sections
Service markings and ammunition type stenciled in faded gray on the receiver
Mounting rail for targeting optics, though most combat operators remove it for weight
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA COMPLIANCE GROUP stamped in gray stencil on the left receiver panel, above the trigger guard. Serial plate (brushed aluminum) mounted on the rear stock with 12-digit identifier and manufacturing date. Warning placards in Mandarin and English on the fuel canister coupling. 'ASHMAKER' designation is field-applied by users, not factory-marked.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but heavily used. Military variants show careful mechanical upkeep alongside visible combat scarring — dents in the polymer from impacts, scorch patterns from nearby blast, heat-stress discoloration throughout. Industrial demolition variants are cleaner but show heavy thermal stress and operator wear. Field weapons typically have jury-rigged reinforcements around the grip and modifications to the radiator system.
